overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals clear viewer preference for extreme cosmic phenomena, bizarre planetary attributes framed through curiosity-driven questions ('What If...'), and high-contrast temporal anomalies. Videos published within the last 7 days targeting exotic planetary conditions and unusual space anomalies (e.g., Venus day length, liquid diamond planets, and extreme dark worlds) dominate views-per-day metrics and secure significantly higher engagement ratios (likes-per-view) than older historical or psychological micro-facts. Conversely, generic psychological tricks, standard animal facts without extreme framing, and older space facts show diminished momentum.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (973 views) exhibit high absolute views and strong engagement within days of publication.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios combined with bizarre, quantifiable planetary anomalies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring stark contrasts or counter-intuitive temporal facts (e.g., 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' with 1,026 views) outperform standard descriptive science titles.
winning_patterns.action: Frame future space and physics facts around impossible-sounding comparisons or sensory paradoxes (e.g., objects colder than ice, sounds that shouldn't exist).

weak_patterns.evidence: Content like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' and psychological song-stuck tricks stagnant under 100 views with negligible engagement.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize standard human psychology micro-facts unless framed as a high-stakes neurological mystery or sci-fi-adjacent thriller.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative animal facts ('Octopuses Have THREE Hearts') show low velocity compared to high-concept cosmic hooks.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content exclusively toward cinematic animal survival or extreme prehistoric context rather than basic trivia.

experiment: Test a 15-second hyper-paced format on a brand-new space anomaly using a rapid zero-to-one hypothetical scenario, comparing initial 48-hour velocity against our baseline planetary 'What If' shorts to test viewer drop-off rates.
